record.paper_title: Open problems on graphs arising from geometric topology
record.original_question: Given any triple of finite graphs K, X, and Y, is there an algorithm that decides whether K is basically embeddable in the product X x Y? In this setting, basic embeddability means that K embeds into X x Y in such a way that each continuous real-valued function on K can be written as a sum of a continuous function of the X-coordinate and a continuous function of the Y-coordinate.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A finite graph is regarded as a one-dimensional topological space (a finite CW complex). Given finite graphs $K$, $X$, and $Y$, an embedding $f:K\hookrightarrow X\times Y$ is called basic if every continuous function $\varphi:K\to\mathbb{R}$ can be represented in the form
$$\varphi(p) = \alpha(\pi_X(f(p))) + \beta(\pi_Y(f(p))) \quad \text{for all } p\in K,$$
for some continuous functions $\alpha:X\to\mathbb{R}$ and $\beta:Y\to\mathbb{R}$, where $\pi_X$ and $\pi_Y$ denote the projections from $X\times Y$ onto its factors. The graph $K$ is said to be basically embeddable in $X\times Y$ if such an embedding exists.

Question: Is there an algorithm that, given any triple $(K,X,Y)$ of finite graphs as input, decides whether $K$ is basically embeddable in $X\times Y$?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches on basic embeddability and decidability of embeddings into products of graphs did not return a result resolving the algorithmic decision problem in the stated generality. Related work addresses embeddability of simplicial complexes (some cases decidable, others undecidable in higher dimensions) and characterizations of basic embeddability into specific products, but no source was found that confirms a decision algorithm or proves undecidability for the general triple $(K,X,Y)$.

status_evidence.title: Invariants of Graph Drawings in the Plane (Skopenkov)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing basic embeddability and related decision problems for graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys on basic embeddings discuss criteria but do not establish a general decision algorithm for triples (K,X,Y).

status_evidence.title: Extendability of Simplicial Maps is Undecidable
status_evidence.snippet: For fixed even l there is no algorithm recognizing extendability of the identity of S^l to a PL map of a given 2l-dimensional complex.
status_evidence.claim: Related undecidability results exist for higher-dimensional embedding/extension problems, but do not directly settle the basic-embedding decision problem for graphs.
